description_full: Ternium S.A., together with its subsidiaries, manufactures and distributes steel products in Mexico, Southern Region, Brazil, and internationally. The company operates through two segments, Steel and Mining. The Steel segment offers slabs, heavy plates, hot and cold rolled products, coated products, stamped steel parts for the automotive industry, roll-formed and tubular products, billets, bars, and other products, including sales of energy. Its Mining segment sells iron ore and pellets. It also provides medical and social; scrap; and engineering and other services. In addition, the company engages in the exploration, exploitation, and pelletizing of iron ore. Ternium S.A. was founded in 1961 and is based in Luxembourg, Luxembourg. Ternium S.A. is a subsidiary of Techint Holdings S.à r.l.

financial_summary: Ternium S.A. Ternium S.A. is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $9.7B market cap on $15.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -2% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.

Returns on capital run at 14% against a 8% cost of capital, a 5-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, and 20% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The company is burning through $345M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
Accruals are elevated at -8.5% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.6× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 3.3×.

Management returns a meaningful 5.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
